Subject: Request: annotated topology + SIG mapping for Dedicated/Private deployments

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the quick answers on the intake form earlier. For our SIG v2 assessment and the SOC 2 evidence pack, Acme needs a concise network assertion that shows:

- an annotated topology (control plane vs data plane) that highlights where customer code and data may ingress/egress for Dedicated and Private modes,
- trust-zone definitions and brief textual justifications per zone,
- a short mapping (table or doc) of SIG questions to the actual artifacts we will hand over, and
- an example security-group / firewall snapshot and an explanation of KMS boundary placement.

Can you provide an "evidence bundle" (PDF diagrams + CSV of SG rules + short mapping doc) and a single-page narrative (one page) that we can attach to the auditor packet? We have a deadline of 2026-12-07 to include this in the final submission.

If it's easier, a Drive folder link + a checklist is fine.

Best,

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-26T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: annotated topology + SIG mapping for Dedicated/Private deployments

Jordan —

Attaching first-pass artifacts into the Drive folder. Summary below; attachments enumerated at the bottom. I focused on clarity for an external auditor who may not be familiar with our infra terminology. Highlights: 

1) Annotated_topology_v2.pdf — single-page topology with legend. Callouts:
   - Control plane: managed control plane (region: us-east-1, us-west-2) lives in a separate management VPC with strict peering rules and an mTLS gateway for API traffic.
   - Data plane (Dedicated): tenant-dedicated GPU pools are provisioned into tenant-specific subnets; shared helper services live in a dedicated shared services VPC. Traffic between tenant subnets and shared services flows over private peering with ACLs.
   - Private deployments: customer-managed VPC peering / transit gateway patterns documented; we explicitly call out optional air-gapped deploys.

2) KMS-boundary-diagram.png — shows where CMK keys are stored (KMS in customer-managed account for Private; Redwood-managed KMS with per-customer key policies for Dedicated hosted by a separate KMS account). Flow annotated for envelope encryption.

3) Controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx — matrix of allowed egress destinations from control plane (DNS, package repos, telemetry endpoints), protocol, and justification; includes S3 endpoints we use for model artifacts and how we restrict access by VPC endpoint.

4) SG-rule-snapshot.csv — sanitized sample rules for Dedicated GPU pool SGs and Private edge proxy (no customer IPs included; ranges redacted). Columns: resource_id, direction, protocol, port_range, cidr, description.

5) sig-mapping.md — short mapping: SIG v2 question IDs -> artifact (diagram page/filename + relevant CSV sheet). I included suggested auditor phrasing for each mapping.

I've kept filenames stable so we can reference them in the auditor email. If you want, I can add a one-page narrative (I can do that tomorrow morning) that condenses the topology and the control rationale.

Attachments placed: annotated_topology_v2.pdf, kms-boundary-diagram.png, controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx, sg-rule-snapshot.csv, sig-mapping.md

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: annotated_topology_v2.pdf (diagram), kms-boundary-diagram.png (png), controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), sg-rule-snapshot.csv (csv), sig-mapping.md (md)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-27T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: annotated topology + SIG mapping for Dedicated/Private deployments

Added an export of current SG rules and a short note on NAT/egress behavior to the Drive folder. Two quick operational notes included in the CSV:

- Dedicated GPU pools: Ingress is limited to load-balancer frontends and internal management hosts; ephemeral worker-to-kv traffic is restricted to internal CIDR and uses signed tokens (no public IPs).
- Egress translation: Private deployments by default rely on customer NAT; for Hosted Dedicated we terminate egress in a dedicated egress VPC with strict proxying and allowlisting.

I redacted any internal jump-host IPs and included a sample iptables-export for one of the worker images in the folder (iptables-sample.txt).

Ben Carter
Senior Cloud Engineer, Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference
